en: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi narrated to me: 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from 'Asim, from 'Amir, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade it only because it was the riding and pack animal of the people, so he disliked that their beasts of burden should be lost, or he declared it unlawful on the day of Khaybar—the meat of domestic donkeys.
And Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated it to me: Hafs—meaning Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us, from 'Asim, with this chain of transmission something similar to it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Asim, from ash-Sha'bi, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded us to throw away the meat of domestic donkeys, both raw and cooked; then he never commanded us to eat it.

Abu Kuraib and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Abu Kuraib said: Ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Thabit ibn 'Ubayd, who said: I heard al-Bara' saying: We were forbidden from the meat of domestic donkeys.

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: al-Bara' said: We obtained donkeys on the day of Khaybar, and the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out: 'Overturn the pots!'

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi—and he is Ibn Thabit—who said: I heard al-Bara' and 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa saying: We obtained donkeys and cooked them, then the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out: 'Overturn the pots!'

Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahid—meaning Ibn Ziyad—narrated to us: Sulayman ash-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa saying: Severe hunger afflicted us during the nights of Khaybar. When it was the day of Khaybar, we fell upon domestic donkeys and slaughtered them. When the pots were boiling with them, the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out: 'Overturn the pots, and do not eat anything of the meat of donkeys!' He said: Some people said: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) only forbade them because the one-fifth (khumus) had not been taken from them.' Others said: 'He forbade them unconditionally.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from ash-Shaybani, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa about the meat of domestic donkeys, and he said: Severe hunger afflicted us on the day of Khaybar while we were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). We captured some donkeys belonging to the people outside the settlement and slaughtered them. Indeed, our pots were boiling when the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out: 'Overturn the pots, and do not eat anything of the meat of donkeys!' I said: 'What kind of prohibition did he forbid them with?' He said: 'We discussed it among ourselves and said: He forbade them unconditionally, or he forbade them because the one-fifth (khumus) had not been taken from them.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: that Abu Idris informed him that Abu Tha'labah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade the meat of domestic donkeys.

Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to me: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abu al-Mundhir al-Qazzaz narrated to us; both of them from Dawud ibn Qays, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dispatched an expedition to the land of Juhaynah and appointed a man over them; and he related the hadith similar to their hadith.

Abu Kuraib narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: al-Walid—meaning Ibn Kathir—narrated to us, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Kaysan saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dispatched a military detachment in which I was included to the seashore. And they all related the rest of the hadith similar to the hadith of 'Amr ibn Dinar and Abu az-Zubayr, except that in the hadith of Wahb ibn Kaysan: 'And the army ate from it for eighteen nights.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Abu Nu'aym Wahb ibn Kaysan: that Jabir ibn 'Abdullah informed him, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dispatched a detachment of three hundred men and appointed Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah as commander over them. Their provisions ran out, so Abu 'Ubaydah gathered their provisions into a bag and rationed it out to us until each one of us would receive a single date each day.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdah—meaning Ibn Sulayman—narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dispatched us, being three hundred men, carrying our provisions on our necks.

'Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: 'Amr heard Jabir saying concerning the Army of Khabat: 'A man slaughtered three camels, then three, then three; then Abu 'Ubaydah forbade him.'

'Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: 'Amr heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dispatched us, being three hundred riders, and our commander was Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, to intercept a caravan of Quraysh. We stayed at the coast for half a month, and severe hunger afflicted us until we ate the leaves beaten down from trees (khabat), so it was called the Army of Khabat. Then the sea threw up for us a sea creature called the 'Anbar (sperm whale). We ate from it for half a month and anointed ourselves with its fat until our bodies returned to health. He said: Abu 'Ubaydah took one of its ribs and set it upright, then looked for the tallest man in the army and the tallest camel and mounted him upon it, and he passed under it. He said: And a group of people sat in the socket of its eye. He said: And we extracted from the hollow of its eye such-and-such number of jars of fat. He said: We had a leather bag of dates with us, and Abu 'Ubaydah used to give each man among us a handful, then he gave us one date by one date; and when it was finished, we felt its loss.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir; (Second Chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Abu Khaythamah reported to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dispatched us and appointed Abu 'Ubaydah as commander over us to intercept a caravan of Quraysh, and he provided us with a leather bag of dates, having found nothing else for us. Abu 'Ubaydah used to give us one date by one date. He said: I asked: 'What did you do with it?' He said: 'We would suck on it as an infant sucks, then drink water after it, and it would suffice us for that day until nightfall. And we used to strike down the leaves of trees (khabat) with our sticks, then moisten them with water and eat them.' He said: We went along the seashore, and something resembling a huge dune appeared before us on the coast. So we went to it, and behold, it was a beast called the 'Anbar (sperm whale). He said: Abu 'Ubaydah said: 'It is carrion.' Then he said: 'No, rather we are the messengers of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and in the path of Allah, and you are compelled by necessity, so eat.' He said: We stayed around it for a month, being three hundred men, until we grew plump. He said: I indeed saw us scooping fat from the socket of its eye in large jars, and cutting pieces of meat from it as large as an ox—or the size of an ox. Abu 'Ubaydah took thirteen men from among us and seated them in its eye socket. And he took one of its ribs and set it upright, then saddled the largest camel with us, and it passed under it. And we prepared strips of cured meat from its flesh as provisions. When we arrived in Medina, we came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and mentioned that to him. He said: 'It is a provision that Allah brought forth for you. Do you have any of its meat with you to give us some to eat?' He said: So we sent some of it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he ate it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym reported to us, from Abu Bishr; (Second Chain) and Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us: Abu Bishr said: he reported to us from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'He forbade...'; (Third Chain) and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to me: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade... with the like of the hadith of Shu'bah from al-Hakam.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us: al-Hakam and Abu Bishr narrated from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade every beast of prey with fangs and every bird with talons.
Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to me: Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us with this chain of transmission the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade every beast of prey with fangs and every bird with talons.
And Abu at-Tahir narrated it to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us: Malik ibn Anas informed me with this chain of transmission the like of it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Rahman—meaning Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us, from Malik, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim, from 'Ubaydah ibn Sufyan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'The eating of every fanged beast among beasts of prey is unlawful.'

And Abu at-Tahir narrated it to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us: Malik ibn Anas, Ibn Abi Dhi'b, 'Amr ibn al-Harith, Yunus ibn Yazid, and others informed me; (Second Chain) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me from 'Abd ar-Razzaq, from Ma'mar; (Third Chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Yusuf ibn al-Majishun reported to us; (Fourth Chain) and al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to us, from Salih; all of them from az-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, like the hadith of Yunus and 'Amr. All of them mentioned 'the eating of' except Salih and Yusuf, for their hadith states: 'he forbade every fanged beast among beasts of prey.'

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Amr—meaning Ibn al-Harith—reported to us: that Ibn Shihab narrated to him, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade the eating of every fanged beast among beasts of prey.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani: that he heard Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade the eating of every fanged beast among beasts of prey. Ibn Shihab said: 'And I had not heard that from our scholars in the Hijaz until Abu Idris narrated it to me, and he was one of the jurists of the people of ash-Sham.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—Ishaq said: he reported to us, and the other two said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Idris, from Abu Tha'labah, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade the eating of every fanged beast among beasts of prey. Ishaq and Ibn Abi 'Umar added in their hadith: az-Zuhri said: 'And we had not heard of this until we arrived in ash-Sham.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from al-'Ala', from Makhul, from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), his hadith regarding hunting. Then Ibn Hatim said: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr and Abu az-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, with the like of the hadith of al-'Ala', except that he did not mention its decaying odor, and he said regarding the dog: 'Eat it after three days, unless it becomes putrid, in which case leave it.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me: Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated to us: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from Abu Tha'labah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) regarding the one who finds his game after three days: 'Then eat it so long as it has not become putrid.'

Muhammad ibn Mihran ar-Razi narrated to us: Abu 'Abdullah Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Abu Tha'labah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'When you shoot your arrow and the game disappears from your sight, then you find it, eat it so long as it has not become putrid.'

Abu at-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us; (Second Chain) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: al-Muqri' narrated to us; both of them from Haywah, with this chain of transmission, similar to the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, except that the hadith of Ibn Wahb did not mention in it hunting with a bow.
